raw_text: We cannot proceed with our enterprise rollout without Okta SAML 2.0 single sign-on. Our corporate InfoSec mandate requires SSO enforcement by end of quarter, or we will be forced to cancel our renewal.
In our security review call today, SAML SSO with Azure AD and Okta was highlighted as a mandatory requirement. Your current username/password login violates our corporate security guidelines.
Is Okta SSO on your near-term roadmap? Our compliance team requires SCIM provisioning and SAML authentication before we can upgrade all 400 seats.
We have a company-wide policy that all third-party SaaS vendors must integrate directly with our Okta identity provider. When will SAML 2.0 be supported?
Our SOC 2 compliance auditor requires all administrative actions, permission changes, and login attempts to be streamed directly to our Datadog and Splunk SIEM via automated audit webhooks.
During the vendor security assessment, our CISO flagged that you do not provide immutable audit log exports. We need streaming audit events for SOC 2 Type II compliance.
We urgently need an automated audit log feed to satisfy our annual security audit. Can you stream login timestamps, IP addresses, and policy changes to our security lake?
The current admin vs member roles are too broad. We need granular role-based access control where contractors can view reports without having export or billing edit permissions.
We have department managers who need to approve workflows without having full administrative rights. Custom permission scopes would solve this completely.
We need read-only auditor roles for our clinical compliance inspectors so they can review historical records without altering any configuration.
When we try to export more than 50,000 records via your REST API, the connection times out after 30 seconds. We need an asynchronous bulk export API with S3 presigned download URLs.
The CSV export fails whenever we select the full year of order data. Can we get scheduled weekly CSV exports sent automatically to email or an SFTP folder?
Yeah, if you could just provide an automated API endpoint for bulk batch exports instead of pagination limits, that would be great. Our analytics warehouse needs daily syncs.
